pages.text: "My bell fell off!" Lulu picked up the blue neck cord in the yard. The knot had opened, and the bell lay in the dirt. Spring wind fluttered the clothesline.
Wanting to tie it alone, Lulu put the cord round the neck and tied hard. Hands off—and it slipped open. "Loose again?" Lulu's ears drooped sadly.
Ten knots, and all ten came loose. Lulu dropped the cord on the dirt and crouched, half hiding a face in the knees. "Only I cannot tie knots."
Aunt Rosa came in a headscarf with an armful of washing. "My cords came loose ten times at first too." With laundry on one arm, she put the cord back in Lulu's hands.
"I make big knots too. Easier to see." She made two loops like rabbit ears. "Around once, pull tight! Make one ear, tuck the other through!"
Lulu tried again. Around once, tight! One ear, the other through! "Done! It stays tied. Once more, nice and tight!"
But hands off—the knot loosened, and the bell fell again. This time Lulu did not throw the cord. "All right. Once more!" Lulu brushed off the dirt.
Around once, tight! One ear, the other through! Now even a tug did not undo it. Lulu shook the neck. Jingle! The bell stayed in place.
Three cousins queued with apron cords. "Mine too, Lulu!" Lulu took the first in both hands. "One, around and tight! Two, two ears! Three, give it a tug!"
Aunt Rosa lifted Lulu and stroked the long ears. Even after ten loose knots, try again and one day it holds tight. Holding a cousin's cord, Lulu called bravely, "Once more, nice and tight!"
